subject: contract-headless-stand
text:
- **Headless stand (seven_guis, native only):** `seven_guis::stand` — `LeanTask { Counter, FlightBooker, Timer, Crud }` with `ALL` and `task()`; pinned `VIEWPORT_WIDTH = 800`, `VIEWPORT_HEIGHT = 600`, `HIDPI_SCALE = 1.0`, `COLOR_SCHEME = ColorScheme::Light`; `font_ctx()` = `build_single_font_ctx(DEJAVU_SANS)`, system fonts off; `options(incremental) -> HarnessOptions` with the pinned viewport and bundled font, `net_provider: None` (offline through `DummyNetProvider`) and `base_url: None`, kept `None` for every caller (unit test `the_stand_options_stay_offline`), so every stand boot is offline but `boot_load`'s, which replaces that one field (below); `boot(LeanTask, HarnessOptions) -> Harness<DioxusDocument>` and `boot_timer(HarnessOptions) -> (Harness<DioxusDocument>, TimerTicks)`, each building a fresh `VirtualDom` whose root provides a `TimerTicks` context and renders `app::task_in_shell` with a no-op back handler; and `TIMER_TICK_MS: u32 = 100` with `timer_step(ticks: TimerTicks) -> impl FnMut(&mut Harness<DioxusDocument>, u32)`, the Timer's time step for a driver session (`Session::with_time`, the Driver session contract below): handed the milliseconds asked, it delivers the whole ticks they hold through `TimerTicks::deliver`, carrying the remainder below one tick across calls (250 then 250 deliver 2 then 3 ticks), and returns nothing — the session, not the step, moves the harness's clock (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); the ticks apply on the next pass (examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:21-129; the time step as measured at escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock/report.md); it installs no telemetry, reads no env var and names no `blitz_net`, its load page's stand-in included.
 Supporting seven_guis API: `app::Task` (pub) and `app::task_in_shell(Task, EventHandler<()>) -> Element`, and `pub fn TaskShell`, the shell a test-local variant of a task mounts in so its unkeyed ids read as the task's (examples/seven_guis/src/app.rs:7; examples/seven_guis/src/app.rs:90; examples/seven_guis/src/app.rs:164); the crate-root `DEJAVU_SANS` woff2 bytes, one `include_bytes!` shared with the wasm entry (examples/seven_guis/src/lib.rs:7; examples/seven_guis/src/lib.rs:17); `tasks::timer::TimerTicks` (`deliver(n)`), which `Timer` reads with `try_use_context` — absent, the 100 ms `futures_timer::Delay` loop; present, one 0.1 s step capped at the duration per delivered tick (examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs:10-20; examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs:47-55)

subject: contract-ci-contracts
intent
text: - **Front page:** the root `README.md` is escher's own page, not upstream Blitz's — what escher is and, since 2026-10-16-handler-splits-and-readme, its state under `## Status`: 0.1.0 done and verified, its six stages listed with three recorded facts (17 capabilities verified, 43 cold-agent tool calls with 0 wrong, 0 surviving mutants of 1,558), and 0.2.0 planned in five stages, one line per epoch of `escher-0.2.0/working-route.md`, where it read built vs planned; the page spells the name «Escher» in its prose and title, crate, binary and path names, URLs and the e-mail unchanged, on the founder's word «чтоб эшер там с большой буквы писался» (2026-10-16) — and since 2026-10-10-driver-cli how the driver's command line is run (the `escher-session` binary: `start`, one driver command per call answering one line of JSON on stdout, the four exit statuses, `stop`), since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface how an MCP client drives the same apps (it spawns `target/debug/escher-session mcp` as its own child and gets the driver commands as tools, the page saying twelve, the count `VERBS` holds), since 2026-10-12-self-description how to ask for `help` on both surfaces, a link to `docs/capabilities.md` as the statement of what Escher can do and its limits (README.md:49), the screenshot no longer named as still to come since 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship, its Blitz lineage, the 0.1.0 epochs, the licence and an Author / Contact section, with the fork's `ci.yml` badge as its one image (README.md). No build or doc step reads it, and one test does — the capability-statement pin reads its count of the driver commands as tools (§Standard Contracts → CI contracts); `rdme` resolves a `README.md` at runtime only (apps/readme/src/main.rs:220-233). At an Upstream sync an upstream change to `README.md` resolves to escher's version (upstream touched it 6 times in the 12 months to 2026-10-06, as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-project-readme/research.md)

subject: intent
text: - **Capability statement:** `docs/capabilities.md` («What Escher can do») is escher's own statement of what it can do, in five sections in order — `## What it can do` · `## Stated limits` · `## Accessibility reach` · `## What an MCP client carries onward` · `## Where each claim is proven`; the CI-script pin `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py` holds its verb and cause names and its five counts — verbs, refusal causes, session errors, node keys, exit statuses — to the driver schema's tables (§Standard Contracts → CI contracts), and no check reads its other claims; README.md links it (README.md:49), and Viola's planning reads it through a pointer in Viola, outside this repository, naming the repository, the path and a commit; no build or doc step reads it
